newsitem.title: BELGIUM: INTERBREW STILL SEEKING PARTNERS FOR SPORTS ASSETS.
newsitem.headline: INTERBREW STILL SEEKING PARTNERS FOR SPORTS ASSETS.

text.p: Belgian brewing giant Interbrew said on Thursday it was still seeking partners for sporting assets owned by its Canadian unit Labatt Brewing Co Ltd, and "a number" of parties were interested.

The assets concerned are Labatt's 90 percent of the Toronto Blue Jays baseball club, its 100 percent of the Toronto Argonauts - a club in the Canadian football league - as well as an interest it holds in Toronto's 50,000-seat SkyDome stadium.
"There are three businesses with different goals and different share holders," said Hugo Powell, Interbrew's chief operating officer for the Americas region.

"We are interested in bringing new partners into those business. We are looking for local partners for them all." Powell said. Until any deals were reached, the priority was to run them well and profitably, he added.
Powell, who was speaking at a presentation of Interbrew's 1996 results, said the value of Labatt's share in the three had been estimated by others at a total of U.S. $185 million.

Interbrew inherited the assets when it bought Labatt, Canada's second-largest brewer, in July 1995. The Belgian group has always said it wanted to concentrate on the core brewing business, though was in no rush to sell the sporting assets and it envisaged retaining the attached marketing rights.
